changes: Every EN 16931 business term can now come from the ERP export: seller and buyer details (trading name, legal registration, address lines 2 and 3, country subdivision, contact), payee, tax representative, deliver to location, invoicing period, VAT point date, VAT in accounting currency, payment means text and code, payment card, SEPA direct debit, document level allowances and charges with base and percentage, rounding amount, VAT exemption reason code, supporting documents with attachments, and on the line the object identifier, line period, price discount and gross price, item classifications and item attributes. The README lists the keys.

tariffCode becomes the item classification with scheme HS, itemAttributes (one 'name: value' per line) and batchNumber become item attributes, itemNote the item description, deliveryTerms and deliveryMode one invoice note, and senderContactEmail the seller contact mail (senderEmail stays the electronic address).
Repeating groups can come as JSON lists: invoiceNotes, precedingInvoices, allowancesCharges, supportingDocuments, and per line itemClassifications and itemAttributes.
A group with a required term missing is left out with a warning instead of producing an invoice the XRechnung validator rejects.
Paid amount (BT-113) for a Schlussrechnung: prepaidAmount lowers the amount due while the totals stay as they are, also from a filled Word invoice.
Amounts written with a decimal comma, such as 100,00, are read as 100 instead of 10000.

Bcc per company: under Outbound > a document type > a company > Goes to > Mail, a Bcc field sits under the Cc. Its addresses get every mail of that company as a blind copy, from the Live ERP and from test systems; the other recipients do not see them.
Live mails also go as a blind copy to the recipientEmailBcc the ERP writes into the export, as its recipientEmailCc already did for Cc. Mails from a test system never go to the ERP's addresses.
An address already in To or Cc is not repeated in Bcc, and every address gets the mail once. An invalid Bcc address is refused when saving and named in the message.

An invoice whose export says eInvoiceType NoEInvoice is no e-invoice: Hive BDC delivers the ERP's PDF as it is, with no XML embedded and no XML file. Until now such an invoice went out as XRechnung XML. Compress PDF applies when it is on.
A blank eInvoiceType still gives XRechnung, as before.

Cc per company: under Outbound > a document type > a company > Goes to > Mail, each company names its own addresses. They get every mail of that company as a copy: Live mails go to the customer or vendor with them in Cc, test mails go to the test recipients with them in Cc.
An address that appears in more than one list (customer, the ERP's Cc, the company's Cc, test recipients) gets the mail once. An invalid address is refused when saving and named in the message.
The test recipients under Connections > Document mail apply to all document types; the web console now calls them Test recipients, as the Windows app does.

Compress PDF, per document type and company under Outbound > Before delivery: each PDF is made smaller once, before it goes to SharePoint, the archive, the output folder and the mail. Fonts keep only the letters used, lossless images placed above 300 ppi are scaled to 200 ppi, identical images and fonts are stored once. Pages look the same; the PDF from the ERP stays as it was.
ZUGFeRD with Compress PDF on: the fonts embedded for PDF/A carry only the letters used. An AX 2009 invoice that only names Arial went from 945 KB to 138 KB in a test.
Signed, encrypted and PDF/A documents, and PDFs that would not get smaller, are delivered as they are; the document history says why.

Windows app: a new outbound document type starts without companies, as in the web console. Until now it took the companies of Sales invoice with their source folder and destinations. Settings already saved stay as they are; remove such a company under its type.

The technical log has a Type filter in the Windows app and the web console: All types, Errors and warnings, Errors, Warnings, Info, Debug and Dashboard actions, with a count of the lines shown. A stack trace shows and hides with its error.
Azure: the Type filter replaces the switch Only warnings and errors. An Info line that mentions an error no longer counts as one. The download is still the whole day.

Inbound flows deliver the CSV to Azure Blob Storage or Azure Service Bus as well as to a folder, for example where a Dynamics 365 F&O receive flow reads; the document file goes beside it, outside the folder the ERP reads. In Blob Storage and Service Bus the CSV has no byte order mark, which F&O would read as part of the first column name.

Azure: the web console has Inbound pages like the Windows app: document types, companies, where the documents come from, where your ERP reads them and the CSV columns with a preview of a ready document. A list the document system leaves empty becomes a text box, so a value no document carries yet can be typed.
Windows: Inbound > Goes to offers Folder the ERP reads, Blob Storage and Service Bus. Preview with a ready document shows the CSV the document makes.

Licences can be bound to one Azure instance. Such a licence runs only on that instance; the set-up assistant shows the Instance ID that Balsoft needs for it, and Service > Licence shows the binding. Licences without a binding work as before.
Azure: the update page no longer stays on "Restarting" when it was opened in 1.8.1 or older; it switches to the new version by itself. The same holds after a return to such a version.
Azure: if a restart takes longer than 6 minutes, the update page says so and offers Reload page.
Azure: after an update, Service > Updates also offers Look now next to Return.

Windows: the dashboard opens again on Windows Server 2016. 1.10.0 waited there forever before its first window, on the fonts of the new look; the same fonts now ship in a form every Windows version reads.

The Windows app is one window in the look of the web console: Overview and Document history under WORK, Outbound, Inbound, Connections and Service under SET UP. The former Settings, history, documents, log, Word check and release notes windows are now pages and dialogs of that window.
Outbound, Inbound, Connections and Service share one Save bar; leaving them with unsaved changes asks first.
The Windows service and the Azure web console work as in 1.9.0.

The web console of an Azure instance is rebuilt on the technology of the other Balsoft web apps (CRM and ERP): the same menu, lists, dialogs and light or dark theme. The Balsoft logo and the name Hive BDC lead back to the overview from every page, and every page has its own address, so a link or a reload opens the same page.

A new instance opens the set-up assistant on the whole screen: the licence, with the tenant ID and the instance address to send to Balsoft and a ready mail, who can do what, where Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations hands over its documents, where they go and a test run. A reload continues at the step reached.
Service has tabs for status, licence, updates and the technical log; the licence file can be dropped onto the page.
When the sign-in of the console ends, the console signs in again by itself instead of showing an error.

E-invoices carry every bank account the ERP lists: each entry of bankAccounts in the export becomes its own payment means in the XML, in the ERP's order, with IBAN, BIC and account holder. An export without the list gives the single account from bankIban as before. An account that is not a valid IBAN is written with payment means code 30 instead of 58.
Windows settings: moving from one company or document type to the next no longer changes the choice of the one shown before (ERP export or Word, Customers or Vendors, E-invoice or PDF).
Otherwise the Windows app and the Windows service work as in 1.8.1.

Hive BDC can run in Azure: a web app in the customer's own subscription, installed as a managed application with a short wizard (region, time zone, sign-in app). Settings are kept in Blob Storage, the document history in Table Storage and every password, key and secret in the instance's own Key Vault. The licence is bound to the tenant of the instance and uploaded in the web console. The Azure Marketplace offer follows.

Web console for an Azure instance, signed in with Microsoft accounts and the roles Viewer, Operator and Administrator: Overview, Document history with Retry, Outbound, Connections and Service, in the same words as the Windows settings. A set-up assistant leads through the licence, the container Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations writes to, the destinations and a test run with the first waiting document. Two administrators who save at the same time do not overwrite each other: the later save is refused and can keep both changes.

Azure Service Bus as a source and a destination: Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations sends each document as a message (queue or topic) with its PDF in a blob container, and results can go back to a queue or topic that an F&O inbound flow reads. Hive BDC signs in with a connection string or, in Azure, as the instance itself.

HTTPS as a destination: each document goes as JSON with its file and fields to a Logic App, a Power Automate flow or your own API. On an Azure instance a web address with its own key can also send documents to Hive BDC.

Updates for Azure instances: Update now on the Service page fetches the signed package from the Balsoft update feed, checks its signature, keeps the settings and can go back to the previous version. Balsoft needs no access to the customer's subscription.

Word invoices keep their layout on servers without Microsoft fonts (an Azure instance runs on Linux): where Arial, Times New Roman, Courier New, Calibri or Cambria is missing, Hive BDC uses the free font with the same character widths that it carries inside the service. Any other missing font is named in the document history. On Windows, regular Cambria text is drawn with that free font too, because Windows keeps this one style in a font collection that Hive BDC does not read; bold and italic Cambria stay Cambria.

Settings in the Windows app: Save keeps the window open and confirms; the destination and connection pages are built from what the service reports, so new kinds appear without a new dashboard. A DocuWare connection of any name now counts as connected.
Known limit: a delivery result sent back to Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations arrives there as an inbound record; F&O does not yet book it on the invoice.
Settings files from 1.5.0 and 1.3.x load unchanged and behave as before; the new options only take effect once they are used.

Settings rebuilt: Outbound (documents from your ERP), Inbound (documents into your ERP), Connections and Service. Each screen holds one level with a breadcrumb back: a document type, its companies, and per company where its documents come from and where they go. Remove asks in the card first, and nothing is written until Save changes.

Several destinations per company: SharePoint, any number of DocuWare file cabinets and mail, each with its own switch that keeps its settings when off. DocuWare documents are stored with typed index values (text, numbers, dates, keywords, tables), and a repeat updates the same document by a match field. Mail and the company itself can be switched on or off per company.

Inbound from DocuWare or SharePoint: documents marked ready (an index field or a library column with a value) become a CSV in the folder the ERP reads, with the document's file if wanted, and are then marked done so they are imported once. The lists in Settings are read from the system itself, and Preview with a ready document shows real values. Further document systems come as connectors with updates.

Document history: every step of every document (received, read, produced, delivered per destination, waiting, failed, done) in plain words, searchable by document number or id, with the documents that need attention and Retry.

Azure Blob Storage: documents Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations writes to a blob container (JSON with a pdfLink PDF) are picked up, and documents can be delivered back to a blob container with a status file (appsettings.json).

Word input: a company entry can take filled Word invoices (.docx) instead of ERP export pairs (Settings, Document types, company entry, Input). Every value is a Word content control tagged with its EN 16931 business term, the lines are a repeating section, and the document's E-Rechnung field chooses XRechnung or ZUGFeRD. Hive BDC builds the same JSON an ERP export writes, makes the PDF itself and delivers as usual.

Built-in Word to PDF renderer: header and footer, paragraphs, nested tables, borders, images and page numbers, without Microsoft Office or Microsoft 365. A PDF saved with the same name next to the .docx is used instead. Documents with text boxes, shapes or other elements the renderer does not draw go to the error folder with the reason.

Word invoices are checked before anything is produced: required fields, and printed totals against the sums of the lines to the cent. A failed file goes to the error folder with a reason file in German and English.

Settings: Word template... saves a generic Word invoice template; Check a Word file... shows the fields, lines, totals check and a PDF preview of a .docx. The documents lists show where each document came from (JSON or Word).

Construction invoices: the invoice types 875, 876 and 877 are accepted (they were written as 380) and keep a deduction line negative. A Leitweg-ID as buyer electronic address (BT-49) is written with scheme 0204. BT-41 (seller contact) and BT-154 (item description) can be set from the export.
Settings files from 1.3.x load unchanged and behave as before; the new options only take effect once they are used.

Header charges from the ERP export (chargeTotalAmount: freight, small-quantity surcharge and other misc charges summed on the header) are written as one document level charge (BT-99) with the reason from chargeReason or "Zuschläge" and the VAT of the header vatCategory and vatRate. The charge counts in the charge total (BT-108), the tax basis (BT-109) and the VAT breakdown, so the e-invoice totals match the printed invoice. Until now the key was logged as not written and the totals were short by the charges.
The line key sellerItemId is recognised as the seller's item number (BT-155, SellerAssignedID), next to itemId and itemNumber.

Settings, Document types: a built-in type you remove stays removed after Save. Until now the service added every missing built-in type back when it loaded the settings, so removed types reappeared. A document the ERP still sends for a removed type goes to the error folder with the reason. Removing every type is refused; untick Enabled instead.
The log shows mail recipients masked (m***@contoso.com) and removes line breaks from values of local API requests, so a request cannot add fake log lines.

The project name from the ERP export (projectName, projektname or projektbezeichnung) is written into the e-invoice next to the project reference (BT-11). Until now that place always said "Project reference". The e-invoice stays valid XRechnung and ZUGFeRD.
Updated the e-invoice library to Balsoft.Hive.EInvoice 1.1.0, which also brings a cryptography component patched for two .NET security advisories (CVE-2026-84008, CVE-2026-70162).

The purchase order reference (BT-13) comes from purchOrderReference whenever the ERP export fills it, then from purchaseOrderReference, then from any other purchase order key. Until now the key that came first in the file won, so a customer field mapping that also sent purchaseOrderReference replaced the customer's purchase order number. The buyer reference (BT-10) is unchanged.

E-invoices carry the legal information of the seller (legal form, seat, register court and number, managing directors) when the ERP export sends it in legalNotice. It is written as an invoice note with subject code REG (BT-22 with BT-21), the place validators check for these details; until now they reported them as missing although the PDF footer showed them.

Settings, Document types: the buttons Add row, Remove, Sample JSON… and Import columns… sit below the column template table. Next to the label they covered "Column templates" when the window was narrower than about 1300 pixels, which includes its default size.
Dashboard (Recent exports) and the Documents window: the Format column is wide enough for "xrechnung" instead of cutting it to "xrechnun".
Settings, Connections: the test recipients start at the top of their box instead of floating in its middle.
Settings, Document types: the Column and Template columns of the column template table are equally wide, so internal names such as Customer_x0020_Number are no longer cut off.
The purchase order reference (BT-13) is also taken from the JSON keys purchOrderReference, purchOrderRef, purchOrderFormNum, purchaseOrderNumber, purchaseOrderId and customerRequisition.
A generic "reference" that equals the invoice number is no longer written as the purchase order reference; the log says why BT-13 stayed empty.
The dashboard's log panel and the All logs window show the newest entry at the top. An error keeps its details (exception and stack trace) directly below it.

Settings, Document types: "Sample JSON…" next to "Import columns…" saves a SharePoint field template file for the selected type and company. It holds the entry's current target and columns, with examples where they are empty; edit it and import it back with "Import columns…".
E-invoice lines can carry a price per base quantity (priceUnit with priceUnitPrice, EN 16931 BT-149): an AX price of 60.45 per 100 pieces is written exactly instead of as a rounded per-piece price.

Line charges and line discounts (lineChargeAmount, lineDiscountAmount with optional reasons, BT-141 and BT-136) are written to the e-invoice, so a line with a surcharge adds up to the ERP's line amount again.

The deliver-to address (deliveryName, deliveryStreet, deliveryPostcode, deliveryCity, deliveryCountry, BG-13) is written; intra-community invoices no longer fail BR-IC-12 for the missing deliver-to country.
A cash discount sent as an amount without a percent gets its percent derived from the gross total; the payment terms no longer read "0 % Skonto".
The unit "st" (AX 2009 Stück) maps to C62 without a warning.

A document type that is disabled no longer has its input folder scanned. The installer default folder (C:\Temp\HiveBDC) on a type you never enabled caused an access error every 30 seconds; a folder shared with an enabled type is still scanned, and a disabled type's pairs dropped there go to the error folder as before.
SharePoint upload on a disabled document type no longer starts the SharePoint connection or shows SharePoint as on. Enabling or disabling a type applies on the next scan without a restart.
Settings, Document types: "Import columns…" moved next to the column templates of the company entry and imports the SharePoint target and columns for exactly that type and company from the file.

First release of Hive BDC (Balsoft Data Connector). It replaces Hive DocFlow: program, service, folders and Setup carry the new name (HiveBDC.exe, the HiveBDC service, C:\Program Files\Balsoft\Hive BDC and C:\ProgramData\HiveBDC).
Hive BDC is installed fresh. Uninstall Hive DocFlow first, then run the Hive BDC Setup and install the new license file from Balsoft (earlier license files are not accepted).
Copy your appsettings.json from the Hive DocFlow folder into the Hive BDC folder before the first start to keep companies, document types, SharePoint and mail settings.
Updates now come from the Hive BDC update feed.
The dashboard shows the version in three parts (1.0.0), the same as the update feed and the release notes.
